title: Insurance Coverage & Patient Responsibility Benefit-Year Accumulators
content:
**Training note — what the deductible met and out-of-pocket met figures belong to.** Accumulators on an Insurance Coverage & Patient Responsibility record belong to the benefit year reckoned by the class's benefit-year basis: a calendar-year class rolls over on January 1, a plan-year class on the anniversary of the record's benefit-year start. Whether the deductible counts toward the out-of-pocket accumulator is likewise a figure of the class.

**Reset.** On the first day of a new benefit year, the deductible met and the out-of-pocket met of the record are each reset to 0.00 by a reset entry equal to the amount accumulated in the year that ended.

**Year an amount belongs to.** Amounts accumulate in the benefit year of the claim line's date of service, not of its posting date, so a line from the prior year adjudicated after the rollover adds to the prior year and does not reduce what the patient owes toward the new year's deductible.

## Questions answered

**When does a Commercial PPO record roll over?** Commercial PPO reckons a plan year, so on the anniversary of the record's benefit-year start — for a benefit-year start of 1 July, on each 1 July.

**When does an Original Medicare Part B record roll over?** On January 1, being a calendar-year class.

**What does the reset entry show?** The amount removed is the amount accumulated in the year that ended. A record that had 283.00 of deductible met on 31 December shows a reset entry of 283.00 on 1 January (hypothetical figures).

**A line with a date of service in December is adjudicated in January — which year does it count toward?** The prior year (December's), for a calendar-year class; it does not reduce what the patient owes toward the new year's deductible.
